chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He said: I asked him about the testimony of women regarding stoning, so he said: If there are three men and two women, and if there are two men and four women, it is not valid for stoning.
ai.seo_question: What is the required ratio of male to female witnesses for stoning in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic consensus that the testimony of women alone, even in larger numbers, is insufficient for the specific punishment of stoning (rajm), which requires a preponderance of male witnesses. It highlights the distinct evidentiary standards in Shia fiqh where the ratio of two women to one man does not suffice for rajm, unlike the general rule for financial transactions, emphasizing the gravity of this capital punishment.
